subject: general
question: What type of coastal plain are the Western Coastal Plains of India classified as?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Submerged Coastal Plain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Western Coastal Plains of India are classified as **submerged coastal plains**, formed due to the submergence of landmass along the western coastline.
 
• This type of plain features narrow coastal strips with lagoons, estuaries, and backwaters commonly found in regions like Kerala.
 
• The submergence of land has resulted in characteristic landforms such as **rivers flowing into the Arabian Sea forming estuaries**, unlike the deltas formed in the eastern coastal plains.
 
• Prominent features of the Western Coastal Plains include **the Konkan Coast (Maharashtra), the Malabar Coast (Kerala), and the Kannad Coast (Karnataka)**.
 
• The submerged nature of the plains makes them rich in aquatic biodiversity, supporting fisheries and other marine activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Submerged Coastal Plain:**

 
 
• These plains are formed when coastal regions sink below sea level due to tectonic movements or rising sea levels.
 
• Submerged plains often feature estuaries, lagoons, and submerged valleys.
 
• Examples include the Western Coastal Plains of India and parts of the eastern United States coastline.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Coastal Plains vs Western Coastal Plains:**
 
 
• Eastern Coastal Plains are emergent plains, characterized by wide deltas of rivers like the Ganga, Godavari, and Krishna.
 
• Western Coastal Plains are submerged plains, with narrow coastal strips and estuaries formed by rivers flowing into the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• **Estuaries:**
 
 
• An estuary is a partially enclosed coastal body of water where freshwater from rivers meets and mixes with saltwater from the sea.
 
• Estuaries are rich in biodiversity and serve as critical habitats for various aquatic species.
 
 
 
• **Backwaters:**
 
 
• Backwaters are brackish lagoons or lakes lying parallel to the coast, formed due to the action of waves and tides.
 
• Kerala is famous for its extensive network of backwaters, such as Vembanad Lake.
